Primary decision point: peering vs Privatelink for egress isolation and regional residency. Agreed to run benchmarks simulating 500 RPS burst, 95th latency target 200ms for inference, and to validate cost projections. transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Sofia Reyes (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (TidalHealth Head of ML Platform), Rita Chan (Cloud Security), Mateo Alvarez (Infra Eng), Devika Patel (Product), Sam O'Neill (CTO)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be rough) ---
Redwood and TidalHealth align on pilot to test private connectivity and residency. Discussed peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs, egress locking, benchmarks (throughput, latency) and success criteria. Action items assigned.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a monday afternoon, um quick roll call?
00:08 Jordan (Customer): Jordan here, hi.
00:09 Rita: Rita.
00:10 Mateo: Mateo.
00:11 Devika: Devika.
00:12 Sam: Sam.
00:14 Alex: Great, i'm Alex from Redwood, priya and daniel are with me and we'll run through scope for the pilot. we want to make sure the SOW captures residency, egress, and bench targets.
00:26 Priya (SE): hi folks, quick agenda: confirm workload sizing, pick connectivity approach (peering vs privatelink), define success metrics and schedule bench runs.
00:35 Jordan: sounds good. our goal is to ensure no data leaves eu-west-1 and to avoid cross-region replication. we've got strict residency requirements for inference.
00:47 Rita: and on top of that, audit logs and KMS keys have to be in our control; we can't have keys outside our tenancy.
00:55 Alex: understood. from Redwood's private offering we can support VPC peering or privatelink-style endpoints; peering gives direct routing but needs route table changes and also potentially transitive routing we need to guard against, privatelink keeps endpoints in your account and is easier for egress control.
01:12 Mateo: if we do peering we need to think about IP overlap, and we already have a few /16s used by older tenants, so that could be tricky.
01:21 Daniel (SE): yeah, ip overlap's a common snag — we usually ask for the CIDR ranges and account IDs up front so our networking team can pre-validate.
01:29 Devika: on success metrics — we want to measure correctness for our clinical NLU pipeline, so token-level hallucination rate below 5% for the prompts we provided and 95th perc latency under 200ms for single-turn inference.
01:45 Priya: okay that helps — for the bench we typically run two profiles: steady-state RPS and burst profile. can you share expected steady and peak rps?
01:54 Jordan: steady 50 rps, peak 500 rps bursts during work hours, mostly short sequences, average prompt length about 120 tokens, max 1024 on some edge cases.
02:06 Priya: good. we should size a pool that can sustain 500 rps bursts with continuous batching and KV cache enabled. also we'll run a quantized variant to estimate cost savings.
02:18 Alex: timeline wise, you said compliance review is around mid-June?
02:23 Sam: yes compliance gating is around june 18th, so ideally pilot starts in mid-may and runs 3 weeks so we have data for your review.
02:32 Alex: ok so proposed timeline: bench and SOW week 1 (this week), infra connectivity week 2, bench runs and validation week 3. works?
02:41 Jordan: yes, that matches our internal timeline.
02:44 Rita: on privatelink — we need to confirm whether the privatelink endpoint will expose any metadata to redwood; we cannot allow PID or PHI to be stored.
02:54 Daniel: we don't store payloads by default in Private; for Private deployments we leave customer data in your VPC and only the control-plane has minimal metadata for tracing; we can extend retention windows but default is ephemeral.
03:05 Rita: can you add that to the security doc? we need explicit statements about no long term storage and audit log retention controls.
03:13 Alex: will do.
03:14 Priya: for benchmarks we'll need a sample prompt set and a small evaluation harness — jordan can you share the prompt set and expected correctness scripts?
03:25 Jordan: yes, i'll share a redacted set by tomorrow, likely removes PHI but keeps the linguistic distribution.
03:30 Mateo: network detail question: is NAT required for egress from our subnets to the redwood service? we want to keep egress locked except to the privatelink endpoint.
03:39 Daniel: with privatelink you can restrict egress to only the endpoint, so no NAT to public internet. with peering you still need to control route tables but traffic stays internal — both can avoid public internet egress but privatelink is simpler for strict egress allow lists.
03:54 Devika: cost concerns — we care about per-token cost. can you estimate cost delta between hosted and private with a dedicated quantized 8-bit model?
04:03 Priya: ballpark: hosting is more op-ex focused, private/dedicated reduces per-token marginal cost when you amortize reserved capacity; quantization can reduce inference GPU memory and may give 20-40% lower token compute cost depending on model. we'll provide a spreadsheet.
04:18 Jordan: great. also, for the bench we want cold-start scenarios and warm-cache scenarios included.
04:23 Priya: yes we'll do cold and warm runs; KV cache warmup is important since many of your flows are session-oriented.
04:31 Alex: on success criteria let's capture these: 1) 95th latency <= 200ms on warm runs; 2) throughput sustaining 500 rps burst with no more than 5% error rate; 3) hallucination rate under 5% on test prompts; 4) security sign-off (KMS keys in customer account, audit logs available).
04:52 Devika: can you also include a target for cost-per-1k tokens to compare to our current vendor?
04:58 Alex: yeah we'll include cost per 1k tokens for baseline and quantized runs.
05:02 Sam: one more enterprise question: routing failover — if a region goes down, what's the recommended fallback? we need to avoid cross-region data leakage.
05:12 Daniel: we can do policy-based routing: fallback to a compatible model in the same region on a different capacity pool; if cross-region fallback is strictly forbidden, we can disable cross-region failover and instead fail closed with retries.
05:25 Rita: we probably will ask for fail closed for the first phase.
05:28 Alex: noted. we'll model both options in the SOW.
05:31 Jordan: about privatelink vs peering decision — seems like security prefers privatelink, infra likes peering for lower operational overhead. can we run a small PoC with both?
05:42 Priya: yes, we can stage it: phase A using privatelink for strict egress and key residency, phase B test peering to compare latencies and ops overhead.
05:51 Mateo: what's involved for peering setup timeline?
05:54 Alex: we'll need CIDRs, account IDs, route table contacts; usually takes 2-3 business days for our network teams to configure and validate.
06:03 Mateo: ok i'll get those.
06:05 Jordan: what metrics will you capture during bench?
06:08 Priya: latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99), token throughput, GPU utilization, batch sizes, cost per token, and per-request correctness score against your reference labels.
06:19 Devika: and can we also capture trace ids to map long tail errors to request shapes?
06:24 Daniel: yes we'll instrument traces, but for PII/PHI we'll redact payloads; traces will include request metadata only.
06:33 Rita: ensure that trace metadata doesn't contain identifiers; we will provide a redaction spec.
06:38 Alex: action items recap — we'll send SOW, bench harness, security doc, and proposed schedule.
06:45 Jordan: ok. any other open items?
06:47 Sam: curious about runtime kernels — will you be using optimized kernels for our model size? we run a 13B model.
06:55 Priya: yes we use kernel selection based on architecture and sequence length; for 13B we have optimized mixed-precision kernels and quantized paths. that will be in our perf notes.
07:06 Devika: how long does a typical bench run take?
07:10 Priya: depends, but full suite (cold + warm + variant quantization + control runs) will take roughly 6-10 hours; we usually do it in an overnight window.
07:20 Jordan: can we coordinate that with your team on the 19th as proposed?
07:23 Alex: yes we'll propose 2027-05-19 as bench day.
07:27 Mateo: final note: we'll need a support channel and escalation path during the pilot.
07:31 Sofia (CSM): i'll set up a slack channel and include on-call rotation for bench day and a shared drive for artifacts.
07:38 Alex: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with SOW and bench harness link.
07:44 Jordan: thanks.
07:45 End of call
